cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses, Israel's leader. He has words He wants spoken over His people, and Moses isn't the one who's supposed to say them. So who gets the job?

cards.question: The LORD wants Moses to pass these words along. Who is Moses supposed to tell?

cards.text: Aaron and his sons, the priests, get the exact words from God: "This is how you are to bless the Israelites." Honestly, THANK YOU, because when I make one up myself it comes out "May your edges be crisp and your middle stay soft."

cards.question: God has handed Aaron and his sons the words of the blessing. How are they supposed to get those words to the Israelites?

cards.text: So here's line one: "May the LORD bless you and keep you;" Short and simple, and I'd stamp it on every cookie if it would fit.

cards.question: Before we hear the rest of the priests' blessing, take a guess. True or false: every line of this blessing is about what the LORD does for His people.

cards.text: Line two: "may the LORD cause His face to shine upon you and be gracious to you;" Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a dark junk drawer, so trust me, light shining on you hits different.
And line three: "may the LORD lift up His countenance toward you and give you peace."

cards.question: In the priests' blessing, lines two and three both picture the LORD's ___ turned toward His people.

cards.text: Three lines, and the LORD in every single one. Then God tells Moses what all this does.

cards.question: When Aaron and his sons speak this blessing, what does God say they're putting on the Israelites?
True or false: in the end, Aaron and his sons are the ones who make the blessing on the Israelites happen.

findings.problem: Card 1 says the LORD has words 'He wants spoken over His people.' This gives away card 4's answer, 'Speak them to the people,' before the baker is asked how the priests are to get the words to the Israelites.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to 'take a guess' about the content of lines two and three before hearing them. Only line one has been told. A baker can't reason out whether every remaining line is about what the LORD does, so the pick comes down to luck about wording they haven't seen.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: Card 7 quotes 'may the LORD cause His face to shine upon you,' which shows the answer 'face' for the fill-in-the-blank on card 9. Card 9 then only asks the baker to repeat a word they just read on screen.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The card is only 'And line three:' plus the verse quote. It has none of Papa Dorin's voice and no context, so the moment is stripped down to a bare reading of the verse.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The first sentence, 'Three lines, and the LORD in every single one,' recaps verses 24-26, which were already told and already asked about on card 6. It doesn't move the passage forward. The card also cites Numbers 6:24-27 for that recap, when the new content it tells is only verse 27.
